idea: LMS, XMSS, SPHINCS+ and Kyber of GmSSL with their tests are 160 KB of code and 99 KB of static data; the link failed by 22 KB.
change: one image per algorithm: suites/gmssl_lms, gmssl_xmss, gmssl_sphincs, gmssl_kyber, sources shared in suites/gmssl/common

idea: GmSSL's Keccak is a compact loop over lanes with byte-wise absorb. Absorb and squeeze directly on the state and call pqc_keccakf1600, so the assembly Keccak applies.
change: suites/gmssl/common/gmssl_port.c (fast_absorb, fast_squeeze and the sha3/shake entry points)
checked: GmSSL kybertest including its ML-KEM-768 vector + fingerprint
note: Encaps 25985 -> 11470, decaps 29632 -> 15114. Assembly Keccak in the image.

idea: Route SM3 through pqc_sm3_compress with leaner buffering, so the faster SM3 of components/prims applies to LMS, XMSS and SPHINCS+.
change: suites/gmssl/common/gmssl_port.c (sm3_init, sm3_update, sm3_finish in fast mode)
note: Regression of 6.6 percent: GmSSL's own unrolled SM3 compression is quicker on this chip than the SM3 backend of components/prims (6191 against 6514 us per 256 blocks). XMSS^MT 20/4 keygen 24823480 -> 26261936.

idea: Time both compression functions when the variant starts and use the quicker one inside the lean buffering.
note: Still 2 percent slower than GmSSL's own sm3_update/sm3_finish: the buffering written here is not leaner on RV32. XMSS^MT 20/4 keygen 24809653 -> 25145396.

idea: If GmSSL's compression is the quicker one, fast mode keeps GmSSL's SM3 as it is; the lean path around pqc_sm3_compress is used only when that backend wins the calibration.
checked: GmSSL lmstest subset on the device + fingerprint (8 equal); host: all four GmSSL test programs in both variants
note: opt equals ref within 0.5 percent for the SM3 algorithms, as intended: before is ref and after is opt of the same run. HSS H5/H5 keygen 17751140 and 17842503. A gain needs an SM3 backend quicker than GmSSL's own.

idea: The first device run of the LMS image ended in a stack protection fault.
note: Not an optimization. GmSSL keeps keys, signatures and contexts in local variables: the HSS test uses 40.8 KB, XMSS^MT signing 29.2 KB.

idea: GmSSL's SPHINCS+ signing has a 131 KB FORS tree as a local variable. A 160 KB job stack could not be allocated (rc = -100); run the SPHINCS+ jobs on a 138 KB static stack instead.
change: suites/gmssl/common/bigstack.c, used by the SPHINCS+ jobs in suite.c
checked: public key fingerprint equal to the host build; host: keygen, sign, verify, reject in both variants
note: Key generation runs on the 138 KB static stack (16.0 s, opt variant; ref not run). Signing does not: the board gave no output for 20 minutes where about 2 minutes were expected, most likely a stack overflow past the static stack, since GmSSL holds FORS trees of 131 KB in local variables. The signing job is no longer started on the device. Verification has no signature to check and was not measured. That run held the board for 20 minutes because of the idle limit it was given.
